items.descriptionOriginal: Υπό την επήρεια μέθης οδηγούσε 42χρονος στην περιοχή της Χαριλάου, στη Θεσσαλονίκη, πραγματοποιώντας επικίνδυνους ελιγμούς με το αυτοκίνητό του. Ο άνδρας, με καταγωγή από τη Γεωργία, συνελήφθη χθες, Πέμπτη 29/10 το βράδυ, ενώ κατά τη σύλληψή του φέρεται να αντιστάθηκε σθεναρά. Από την αστυνομική έρευνα διαπιστώθηκε ότι δεν διέθετε άδεια οδήγησης ούτε έγγραφα που να δικαιολογούν τη νόμιμη παραμονή του στη χώρα. Εις βάρος του σχηματίστηκε δικογραφία για απείθεια, βία κατά υπαλλήλων και παραβάσεις της νομοθεσίας περί αλλοδαπών και του ΚΟΚ.

items.title: «Γίνε εθελοντής δότης μυελού των οστών» – Εκδήλωση ενημέρωσης από τον Σύλλογο RED-Y στη Θεσσαλονίκη

items.descriptionOriginal: Ο σύλλογος RED-Y διοργανώνει στον πεζόδρομο της Αγίας Σοφίας στη Θεσσαλονίκη εκδήλωση ευαισθητοποίησης και ενημέρωσης του κόσμου γύρω από τους εθελοντές δότες μυελού των οστών. Η ιδρύτρια του συλλόγου, Αφροδίτη Νέστορα , μιλώντας στην ΕΡΤ3 και την εκπομπή « Μέρα με Χρώμα » αναφέρθηκε στη συγκεκριμένη δράση αλλά και στο μήνυμα, που θέλει να περάσει ο σύλλογος RED-Y. «Η εκδήλωση πραγματοποιείται μία μέρα πριν την επίσημη έναρξη της ενιαίας ψηφιακής πλατφόρμας «Επόπτης», η οποία στην ουσία θα συντονίζει 127 αιμοδοσίες. Είναι πολύ σημαντικό το βήμα αυτό. Ήταν ένα πάγιο αίτημα και του δικού μας σωματείου, που ασχολείται, μεταξύ άλλων, και με τις εθελοντικές αιμοδοσίες. Είναι πολύ σημαντικό ανά πάσα στιγμή να γνωρίζουμε τα αποθέματα αίματος στη χώρα μας και γι’ αυτό τον λόγο θα πρέπει να συμμετέχουμε και να ενισχύουμε την εθνική προσπάθεια, που γίνεται. 124 νοσοκομεία θα δώσουν ό,τι στοιχεία έχουν στη διάθεσή τους προκειμένου να γίνει μία συντονισμένη προσπάθεια. Σε 74 νοσοκομεία θα γίνει αναβάθμιση των συστημάτων, που υπάρχουν και σε 24 νοσοκομεία θα μπουν νέα συστήματα για τα θέματα της αιμοδοσίας», ανέφερε χαρακτηριστικά. items.title: Ο μηχανισμός κατανομής της χοληστερόλης δείχνει έναν πιθανό νέο στόχο για τη θεραπεία του καρκίνου του παγκρέατος
items.titleOriginal: Cholesterol-sharing mechanism points to potential new target for pancreatic cancer treatment
items.description: Οι ερευνητές του Fox Chase Cancer Center εντόπισαν έναν πιθανό θεραπευτικό στόχο για τον καρκίνο του παγκρέατος αφού έδειξαν ότι η ανάπτυξη του όγκου μπορεί να επιβραδυνθεί και η καταστολή του ανοσοποιητικού μπορεί να μειωθεί σε προκλινικές δοκιμές αναστέλλοντας μια συγκεκριμένη πρωτεΐνη, που ονομάζεται ανοκταμίνη 6 (ANO6).
items.descriptionOriginal: Fox Chase Cancer Center researchers identified a potential therapeutic target for pancreatic cancer after showing that tumor growth can be slowed and immune suppression can be reduced in preclinical trials by blocking a particular protein, called anoctamin 6 (ANO6).

items.descriptionOriginal: Ο Ντιέγκο Μαραντόνα δεν χρειαζόταν παρά μια μπάλα για να αλλάξει τον κόσμο γύρω του. Με το αριστερό του πόδι μπορούσε να διαλύσει τις βεβαιότητες των αντιπάλων, να καταργήσει τις αποστάσεις, να μετατρέψει μια συνηθισμένη ποδοσφαιρική αναμέτρηση σε παράσταση που θα έμενε για πάντα στη μνήμη. Γεννημένος, σαν σήμερα (30 Οκτωβρίου) το 1960, στις φτωχογειτονιές του Μπουένος Άιρες, έφτασε στην κορυφή του παγκόσμιου ποδοσφαίρου χωρίς να αποβάλει από πάνω του τη σκόνη της καταγωγής του. Δεν ήταν ο αθλητής που εντυπωσίαζε μόνο με την τεχνική του, ούτε ο σταρ που έμαθε να διαχειρίζεται τη δημοσιότητά του. Ήταν ένας δημιουργός που έμοιαζε να αυτοσχεδιάζει πάνω στο χορτάρι, σαν μουσικός της τζαζ που αψηφά την παρτιτούρα και ανακαλύπτει κάθε φορά μια καινούργια μελωδία. Η μπάλα γινόταν προέκταση του σώματός του, οι ντρίμπλες του μικρές επαναστάσεις απέναντι στη λογική και το γκολ μια πράξη ελευθερίας. Οι αντίπαλοι έβλεπαν μπροστά τους έναν ποδοσφαιριστή και συχνά κατέληγαν να κυνηγούν μια σκιά. Οι θεατές δεν παρακολουθούσαν απλώς έναν αγώνα· περίμεναν την επόμενη στιγμή μαγείας. Ο Μαραντόνα είχε την ικανότητα να κάνει το αδύνατο να μοιάζει φυσικό και το απίθανο αναπόφευκτο. Αυτή ήταν η αγωνιστική του ιδιοφυΐα. Δεν έπαιζε απλώς καλύτερα από τους άλλους. Έδινε την εντύπωση πως έβλεπε ένα διαφορετικό παιχνίδι, σε ένα γήπεδο όπου οι υπόλοιποι δεν είχαν ακόμη ανακαλύψει όλες τις διαστάσεις του. Κι όταν η ποδοσφαιρική του διαδρομή έφτασε στο απόγειό της, αποδείχθηκε ότι η επιρροή του δεν περιοριζόταν στους έντεκα παίκτες που παρατάσσονταν απέναντί του. Ο Ντιέγκο είχε αρχίσει να γίνεται κάτι πολύ μεγαλύτερο από έναν αθλητικό ήρωα. EPA/BORIS ROESSLER Το 1984, εγκαταλείποντας την Μπαρτσελόνα, ο Μαραντόνα θα μπορούσε να επιλέξει έναν ακόμα μεγάλο ευρωπαϊκό σύλλογο, να παραμείνει στο κέντρο της ποδοσφαιρικής βιτρίνας και να διεκδικήσει τίτλους σε ένα περιβάλλον που διέθετε χρήματα, αίγλη και καθιερωμένο κύρος. Προτίμησε τη Νάπολη. Η απόφασή του είχε κάτι από εκείνες τις επιλογές που, εκ των υστέρων, μοιάζουν να υπακούουν σε μια αόρατη ιστορική αναγκαιότητα. Η πόλη του ιταλικού Νότου κουβαλούσε τη φτώχεια, την κοινωνική περιφρόνηση και το αίσθημα της διαρκούς υποβάθμισης απέναντι στον πλούσιο Βορρά. Οι κάτοικοί της είχαν συνηθίσει να αντιμετωπίζονται ως οι φτωχοί συγγενείς μιας χώρας που δεν τους αναγνώριζε πάντοτε ως ισότιμους. Κι εκεί εμφανίστηκε ένας Αργεντινός που δεν έμοιαζε να ενδιαφέρεται για τις καθιερωμένες ιεραρχίες. Δεν πήγε στη Νάπολη για να ολοκληρώσει μια ήδη επιτυχημένη καριέρα. Πήγε για να δημιουργήσει κάτι που δεν είχε προηγούμενο. Η άφιξή του προκάλεσε ενθουσιασμό που ξεπερνούσε την υποδοχή ενός μεγάλου ποδοσφαιριστή. Οι άνθρωποι έβλεπαν στο πρόσωπό του έναν δικό τους άνθρωπο, έναν φτωχό που είχε φτάσει στην κορυφή χωρίς να αρνηθεί τις ρίζες του. Η καταγωγή του δεν αποτελούσε λεπτομέρεια του βιογραφικού του, αλλά μέρος της ταυτότητάς του. Γι’ αυτό και η σχέση του με την πόλη απέκτησε σχεδόν οικογενειακή διάσταση. Ο Μαραντόνα δεν ήταν ένας ξένος που ήρθε να προσφέρει θέαμα και να φύγει. Έγινε ο Ντιέγκο της Νάπολης, το πρόσωπο μέσα από το οποίο μια ολόκληρη κοινωνία μπορούσε να αναγνωρίσει τη δική της αξιοπρέπεια. Ήταν ίσως η μοναδική περίπτωση ποδοσφαιριστή που μετατράπηκε σε τέτοιο κοινωνικό φαινόμενο ακριβώς επειδή δεν επέλεξε την ευκολότερη διαδρομή προς τη δόξα, αλλά μια πόλη που είχε περισσότερο ανάγκη από έναν ήρωα παρά από έναν σταρ. Οι τίτλοι που ακολούθησαν έδωσαν στην επιλογή του ιστορική διάσταση. Ο Μαραντόνα οδήγησε τη Νάπολι στην κατάκτηση του πρώτου της πρωταθλήματος το 1987, επανέλαβε τον θρίαμβο το 1990, κατέκτησε το Κύπελλο Ιταλίας και το Κύπελλο UEFA το 1989. Η ομάδα που μέχρι τότε κοιτούσε τους μεγάλους από απόσταση έγινε πρωταγωνίστρια και ανάγκασε τους ισχυρούς να αναγνωρίσουν τη δύναμή της. Κάθε νίκη είχε τη σημασία μιας συμβολικής ανατροπής. Κάθε τρόπαιο ήταν μια απάντηση στην περιφρόνηση, μια στιγμή κατά την οποία οι άνθρωποι του Νότου μπορούσαν να πανηγυρίζουν χωρίς να αισθάνονται κατώτεροι. Ο Μαραντόνα δεν εξαφάνισε τη φτώχεια, ούτε άλλαξε τις κοινωνικές δομές της Ιταλίας. Έδωσε, όμως, σε εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες ανθρώπους κάτι που η καθημερινότητα συχνά τούς στερούσε: την πεποίθηση ότι μπορούσαν να νικήσουν εκείνους που θεωρούσαν ανώτερους. Για λίγες ώρες, οι απογοητεύσεις, οι στερήσεις και οι ταπεινώσεις υποχωρούσαν μπροστά στη χαρά μιας κοινής νίκης. Το όνομά του ακουγόταν στους δρόμους, στα σπίτια, στις πλατείες, στις εκκλησίες. Η εικόνα του έγινε μέρος της ταυτότητας της πόλης, σχεδόν ένα οικογενειακό κειμήλιο που περνούσε από γενιά σε γενιά. Στη Νάπολη, ο Μαραντόνα δεν αγαπήθηκε μόνο επειδή ήταν ο καλύτερος ποδοσφαιριστής που είχαν δει ποτέ. Αγαπήθηκε επειδή έκανε τους κατοίκους της να αισθάνονται πως η δική τους πόλη μπορούσε να βρίσκεται στην κορυφή χωρίς να ζητήσει την άδεια κανενός. Η ποδοσφαιρική του αξία μετατράπηκε σε κοινωνικό κεφάλαιο και η αγωνιστική επιτυχία σε συλλογική υπερηφάνεια. Αυτό είναι το σπάνιο προνόμιο του Μαραντόνα: να κερδίζει τίτλους για μια ομάδα και, ταυτόχρονα, να προσφέρει σε μια ολόκληρη κοινωνία έναν διαφορετικό τρόπο να βλέπει τον εαυτό της. Δεν ήταν απλώς ο άγιος της Νάπολης. Ήταν ο άνθρωπος που έδωσε στον λαό της το δικαίωμα να αισθάνεται βασιλιάς. Διαβάστε ακόμα Το 1986, στο Παγκόσμιο Κύπελλο του Μεξικού, η προσωπική του ιδιοφυΐα απέκτησε εθνικές διαστάσεις. Ο Μαραντόνα πήρε την Αργεντινή από το χέρι και την οδήγησε στην κατάκτηση του τροπαίου, πραγματοποιώντας μια από τις μεγαλύτερες ατομικές παραστάσεις στην ιστορία της διοργάνωσης. Στον προημιτελικό με την Αγγλία πέτυχε δύο γκολ που συμπύκνωναν ολόκληρη την αντιφατική του φύση. Το πρώτο, με το περίφημο «χέρι του Θεού», παραβίασε τους κανόνες και προκάλεσε ατέλειωτες συζητήσεις. Το δεύτερο ήταν ένα ποδοσφαιρικό αριστούργημα: ο Μαραντόνα ξεκίνησε την επέλασή του από τη μεσαία γραμμή, πέρασε τον έναν αντίπαλο μετά τον άλλο και έστειλε την μπάλα στα δίχτυα, σαν να είχε αποφασίσει ότι κανείς δεν θα μπορούσε να σταθεί εμπόδιο στη διαδρομή του. Η αναμέτρηση είχε ιδιαίτερο συμβολισμό. Τέσσερα χρόνια νωρίτερα, ο πόλεμος των Φόκλαντ είχε τελειώσει με την ήττα της Αργεντινής από τη Μεγάλη Βρετανία, αφήνοντας πίσω του νεκρούς και ένα βαθύ εθνικό τραύμα. Η νίκη επί της Αγγλίας δεν αναίρεσε την ιστορική πραγματικότητα ούτε αποκατέστησε τις απώλειες. Έδωσε, όμως, σε έναν πληγωμένο λαό μια στιγμή συμβολικής δικαίωσης. Το ποδόσφαιρο έγινε η σκηνή πάνω στην οποία μπορούσε να εκφραστεί μια συσσωρευμένη ανάγκη περηφάνιας. Μετά την πρόκριση επί της Αγγλίας, η Αργεντινή κατέκτησε το Παγκόσμιο Κύπελλο και ο αρχηγός της πέρασε στην ιστορία. Ο Μαραντόνα δεν ήταν απλώς ο κορυφαίος παίκτης μιας πρωταθλήτριας ομάδας. Έγινε η ενσάρκωση της εθνικής αυτοπεποίθησης, ένας ήρωας που επέστρεψε στον λαό του την πίστη στη δυνατότητα της νίκης. Όπως στη Νάπολη, έτσι και στην Αργεντινή, η αξία του ξεπέρασε την αγωνιστική επίδοση. Η μπάλα στα πόδια του έγινε κάτι περισσότερο από όργανο ενός παιχνιδιού: έγινε σύμβολο αξιοπρέπειας, αντίστασης και δικαίωσης. Ελάχιστοι αθλητές στην ιστορία κατάφεραν να συνδέσουν το ταλέντο τους με τη συλλογική μνήμη ενός λαού σε τέτοιο βαθμό. Ο Μαραντόνα το πέτυχε επειδή δεν έμοιαζε αποκομμένος από τους ανθρώπους που τον αποθέωναν. Η διαδρομή του, από τη φτώχεια στην παγκόσμια κορυφή, ήταν και η δική τους ιστορία. Η κοινωνική και πολιτική του ταυτότητα συμπλήρωνε αυτήν την εικόνα. Ο Μαραντόνα δεν έκρυβε τις αντιπάθειές του ούτε προσπαθούσε να εμφανίζεται ουδέτερος για να διατηρεί την αποδοχή όλων. Καταφερόταν εναντίον του πλούτου και της πολυτέλειας του Βατικανού, αντιπαραβάλλοντας την εικόνα της χλιδής με την εξαθλίωση των φτωχών. Μιλούσε ανοιχτά για τη φιλία και την εκτίμησή του προς τον Φιντέλ Κάστρο και τον Λουίς Ινάσιο Λούλα ντα Σίλβα, ενώ τα τατουάζ του Τσε Γκεβάρα και του Κάστρο δήλωναν τις πολιτικές του αναφορές. Δεν ήταν πολιτικός θεωρητικός, ούτε η ζωή του αποτελούσε υπόδειγμα συνέπειας. Είχε, ωστόσο, το θάρρος να εκφράζει δημόσια τις πεποιθήσεις του, χωρίς να υπολογίζει πάντοτε το κόστος. Δεν επιδίωξε να γίνει αρεστός σε όλους. Προτιμούσε να συγκρούεται με εκείνους που θεωρούσε εκπροσώπους της αδικίας, ακόμα κι όταν οι απόψεις του προκαλούσαν αντιδράσεις. Η στάση του δεν ήταν απαλλαγμένη από αντιφάσεις, αλλά αυτό δεν αναιρεί τη σημασία της κοινωνικής του απήχησης. EPA/CEZARO DE LUCA Ο Μαραντόνα εξέφραζε μια βαθύτερη επιθυμία των ανθρώπων που ξεκινούν από χαμηλά: να μην χρειάζεται να απολογούνται για την καταγωγή τους, να μπορούν να αμφισβητούν τους ισχυρούς και να διεκδικούν τη θέση τους στον κόσμο. Γι’ αυτό και η λατρεία προς το πρόσωπό του δεν περιορίστηκε στα γήπεδα. Απλώθηκε σε κοινωνίες και γενιές που έβλεπαν σε εκείνον, όχι μόνο έναν μοναδικό ποδοσφαιριστή, αλλά και έναν άνθρωπο που δεν αποδέχθηκε τον ρόλο που του είχε προκαθορίσει η κοινωνική του αφετηρία. EPA/STRINGER Η ζωή του, βέβαια, είχε και σκοτεινές πλευρές. Οι εξαρτήσεις και οι αυτοκαταστροφικές επιλογές του τραυμάτισαν την πορεία του και τον έφεραν αντιμέτωπο με σοβαρά προβλήματα υγείας. Δεν υπάρχει λόγος να εξωραΐζονται ούτε να παρουσιάζονται ως παράδειγμα προς μίμηση. Δεν αποτελούν, όμως, το μέτρο με το οποίο πρέπει να κριθεί το σύνολο της ιστορικής του παρουσίας. Οι αδυναμίες του δεν ακυρώνουν όσα πέτυχε, ούτε εξαφανίζουν τη σημασία που απέκτησε για εκατομμύρια ανθρώπους. Ο Μαραντόνα δεν υπήρξε άγιος. Δεν χρειαζόταν να είναι. Ο θάνατός του, στις 25 Νοεμβρίου 2020, σε ηλικία εξήντα ετών, δεν έβαλε τέλος στην ιστορία του. Αντίθετα, άνοιξε έναν νέο κύκλο συζητήσεων για τις συνθήκες της ιατρικής φροντίδας του και τις ευθύνες όσων βρίσκονταν κοντά του, ζητήματα που αποτέλεσαν αντικείμενο δικαστικής διερεύνησης. Η απώλειά του προκάλεσε συγκίνηση σε ολόκληρο τον κόσμο, από το Μπουένος Άιρες μέχρι τη Νάπολη, όπου οι άνθρωποι αποχαιρέτησαν όχι μόνο έναν ποδοσφαιριστή, αλλά ένα κομμάτι της προσωπικής και συλλογικής τους ιστορίας. Γιατί ο Μαραντόνα δεν ήταν ακόμα ένας πρωταθλητής που αποσύρθηκε από τη σκηνή και παραχώρησε τη θέση του στους επόμενους. Ήταν μια μορφή που άλλαξε τον τρόπο με τον οποίο αντιλαμβανόμαστε τη σχέση ανάμεσα στον αθλητισμό, την κοινωνία και την ταυτότητα. Η αγωνιστική του μεγαλοσύνη θα κρίνεται πάντα από τις ντρίμπλες, τα γκολ, τους τίτλους και εκείνες τις στιγμές που έκαναν το ποδόσφαιρο να μοιάζει με τέχνη. Η ιστορική του σημασία, όμως, βρίσκεται και αλλού: στο πώς κατάφερε να γίνει η φωνή ανθρώπων που σπάνια βρίσκονταν στο επίκεντρο, το σύμβολο μιας πόλης που διεκδίκησε την περηφάνια της και ο ήρωας ενός λαού που αναζήτησε μέσα από το ποδόσφαιρο τη συμβολική του δικαίωση. Οι προσωπικές του αδυναμίες δεν εξαφανίζονται από τη βιογραφία του, αλλά δεν δικαιούνται να καταλάβουν τη θέση που ανήκει στα επιτεύγματά του. Η ιστορία δεν απαιτεί από τους μεγάλους να είναι αψεγάδιαστοι. Απαιτεί να κατανοούμε τι άλλαξαν στον κόσμο. Και ο Μαραντόνα άλλαξε πολλά περισσότερα από τα αποτελέσματα αγώνων. Στη Νάπολη, το όνομά του παραμένει συνδεδεμένο με την εποχή που η πόλη κοίταξε τους ισχυρούς στα μάτια. Στην Αργεντινή, με τον άνθρωπο που σήκωσε το Παγκόσμιο Κύπελλο και έγινε η ενσάρκωση μιας εθνικής υπερηφάνειας. Στην παγκόσμια ποδοσφαιρική μνήμη, με τον παίκτη που μπορούσε να μετατρέψει μια μπάλα σε έργο τέχνης και μια ατομική ενέργεια σε κοινό βίωμα. Ο Ντιέγκο Μαραντόνα δεν χρειάζεται να ανακηρυχθεί άγιος για να παραμείνει μεγάλος. Του αρκεί εκείνη η μαγική διαδρομή προς τα δίχτυα, εκείνο το αριστερό πόδι που έκανε εκατομμύρια ανθρώπους να σηκωθούν από τις θέσεις τους, εκείνη η φανέλα που έγινε σημαία για όσους ένιωθαν πως ο κόσμος τούς είχε ξεχάσει. Οι άνθρωποι πεθαίνουν, τα σώματα χάνονται, οι εποχές αλλάζουν. Αλλά κάποια γκολ δεν τελειώνουν ποτέ. Συνεχίζουν να ταξιδεύουν από γενιά σε γενιά, σαν φλόγες που περνούν από χέρι σε χέρι μέσα στη νύχτα. Κι όσο ένα παιδί στη Νάπολη θα ονειρεύεται να γίνει ο Ντιέγκο κι ένας Αργεντινός θα σηκώνει το βλέμμα του προς τον ουρανό θυμούμενος το Μεξικό του 1986, ο Μαραντόνα θα παραμένει εκεί: όχι απλώς ως ο μεγαλύτερος ποδοσφαιριστής, αλλά ως ο άνθρωπος που έκανε τους περιφρονημένους να αισθανθούν ανίκητοι. items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Generates Clean Energy, Saves Land, Improves Fishing—What’s Not to Like? Reading Time: 2 minutes In September 2026, solar developer D3 Energy installed a large solar array, not on land or on a rooftop, but on the surface of a reservoir that serves the water needs of the village of Monroeville, Ohio. This floating power plant covers 12 acres of the reservoir’s 16 acres. If a solar facility of this size, which contains 9,220 solar panels, were built on dry land, it would require 30 acres. So doing it the Monroeville way helps to keep open land available for farming, housing, business or industry, conservation land, or any other use. This 6-megawatt installation is projected to generate about 7,500 megawatt-hours of clean electricity to this village of 1,300 residents. Monroeville has already operated a 4-megawatt ground-mounted solar array, built in 2017. This 10-megawatt total gives the town roughly 13 times as much solar-generated power per capita as the rest of Ohio. Their floating solar array is among the five largest in the U.S. In addition to the clean power produced and the avoidance of using land that might be put toward other needed uses, Floato-voltaics projects such as this one have several other benefits. First, the physical barrier created by the floating platforms significantly reduces water evaporation by blocking direct solar radiation and intercepting wind blowing across the water’s surface. Solar “on the water” thereby reduces evaporation by 30% to 80%, depending on temperatures and humidity in the immediate area. The result, depending upon the size of the floating power plant, is an annual savings of millions of gallons of valuable drinking and irrigation water. Beyond clean power, floating solar arrays like Monroeville’s reduce reservoir water evaporation by 30% to 80% by blocking direct solar radiation and wind, saving millions of gallons of drinking and irrigation water annually. Photo courtesy of D3 Energy . Second, by depriving the water of sunlight, there is a sizable reduction of toxic algal blooms. Photosynthetic organisms like blue-green algae require sunlight to thrive. By heavily shading parts of the reservoir, the concentrations of floating solar panels limit the light penetration needed for massive algal blooms. This naturally improves water quality, reducing expenses from chemical treatments needed to purify the water. Third, more fish. During the warmer months, the floating platforms insulate the reservoir’s water against seasonal temperature spikes, helping support cold-water fish species. Local reservoirs are often favorite local fishing spots. And fourth, cleaning issues. Land-based solar arrays, whether in farming or more urbanized areas, often deal with dust, dirt, and other airborne debris. For best panel performance, cleaning of their surfaces in these situations is advisable. Open bodies of water are inherently less affected by blowing dirt and dust, keeping the panels cleaner longer and reducing maintenance costs. All things considered, with all the bodies of fresh water dotting the planet, maybe we should all look more closely for floato-voltaic opportunities just beyond our own backyard. The post Generates Clean Energy, Saves Land, Improves Fishing—What’s Not to Like? appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: I n the early-ish days of Wikipedia, my college friends and I had an ongoing contest to see who could introduce a lie into an entry that would stick the longest. If your goal is to smuggle mistruth into the internet’s encyclopedia, you quickly learn to leave the well-known stuff with hard-and-fast facts alone. Try to change the Battle of Hastings to 1068, or claim Thomas Jefferson wrote Flowers for Algernon , and the Wiki editors swoop in to excise your lies within minutes. It was oddly inspiring to see that the online compulsion to be right, and for things to be right, could become a kind of immune system for upholding the truth. Observing the editors’ behaviors, I conjured up a new strategy. I found a less-trafficked page — the entry for club sandwich — and located a sentence that was already conjecture, and which notably had a citation affixed to its end. The line read: It is thought that the club sandwich was invented in an exclusive Saratoga Springs, New York gambling club in the late 19th Century. I changed this by adding my buddy Danny as the sandwich’s inventor: It is thought that the club sandwich was invented in an exclusive Saratoga Springs, New York gambling club in the late 19th Century by a maverick line cook named Danny Mears. It’s unlikely that John McPhee had stumbled across our Wikipedia sandwich lie when he wrote that “any error is everlasting” in his 2009 New Yorker piece about the magazine’s fact-checking department. But he was right. “Maverick line cook Danny Mears” hardened into sturdier fiction with each repetition, appearing in poorly researched blog posts and online recipes, each mention making the lie seem more true. Wiki editors pulled it down a few times; we snuck it back in. In the end, Mears’ reign as the sandwich’s inventor persisted on Wikipedia for more than three-and-a-half years. An annoyed editor even added a Wiki “talk” comment exposing our misdeeds, titled Danny Mears Did Not Invent It . A couple years later, a friend texted the group to say she’d seen “maverick line cook Danny Mears” go up on the flatscreens as a bar-trivia answer. McPhee goes on to describe the job of fact-checking as a kind of noble guardian, holding back a teeming horde of mistruths: “With drawn sword, the fact-checker stands near the end of this bridge.” We’d camouflaged our lie past a few of these sentries for what amounted to a joyride, but eventually the guards got us. What I’ve been wondering ever since, and especially lately, is: Who’s still guarding that bridge? O ne may initially concede that our defenses seem to be diminishing in the present moment. You don’t have to look far to find a commentator mourning a “post-fact” world or worrying that we swim in toxic waters online when it comes to bad actors and misinformation. Consider that 20 percent of Americans surveyed by Pew Research said they regularly get their news from TikTok, up from three percent in 2020. Last year, Meta ended its U.S. fact-checking program, while the courts have decided that social media platforms are private providers of forums for speech and so can set their own content rules, or remove the guardians from the bridge entirely, depending on their business incentives. Credit: patpitchaya / Shutterstock There are few forces more powerful in the media than a stubborn person on the phone investigating a doubt. In the public sphere of reportage, Duke Reporters’ Lab, which has tracked fact-checking trends for years, found that last year was the first time fact-checking department closures outpaced launches . And on the level of the individual, three-fourths of the fact-checkers surveyed by the International Fact-Checking Network reported being financially vulnerable or in crisis . If the field has had a famous debunker in the last two decades, it has been t he Washington Post ’s Glenn Kessler, who last year accepted a buyout and was not replaced. Should you want to pre-write a eulogy for the capital-T Truth, the material is all here. But fact-checking is not a static field. Like our immune systems, it’s capable of learning and enduring, as well as mobilizing to handle infections of mistruth, which if not treated tend to further polarize voters in political contests. Consider recent false claims from his opponents that Texas Senate candidate James Talarico had disappeared from the campaign trail for mental health treatment at an inpatient facility in Ohio. A high-profile fact-check quickly shifted the narrative from “Talarico is in trouble” to “his opponents look like liars.” (Talarico had the flu and was resting at home, which the New York Times proved by reviewing security camera footage.) Bad-faith punditry has a lessened effect when met with undeniable facts and data, as do the rumors that chip away at our trust in elections themselves. Consider a recent viral video in which a woman from Cook County, Illinois claimed that her voting machine was telling her that her chosen candidate was the less-popular choice. Nonpartisan fact-checks from places like PolitiFact quickly rushed to explain the less-salacious reality: She hadn’t selected enough candidates. Fact-checks can bring the temperature down and reduce our polarization; her town’s Republican Committeeman even rose to refute the claims on Facebook . So while the institutional layer of the media is wounded and we’re ushering in an age of slop and lies, any obituary for the Truth is likely premature. Weighed down by negative news? Enter your email below to receive our smart, uplifting newsletters. Or click here to choose exactly which ones you want [contact-form-7] “Ever since I was a little kid, I’ve had a thing about wanting to get stuff right,” says Jy Murphy, a freelance fact-checker for the Hearst stable of publications and others. “At this point it bleeds over as a kind of professional deformity.” Murphy tells a simple story set years ago, in which he was fact-checking a Popular Mechanics piece about the freight industry and encountered a confident sentence claiming that nobody double-stacks rail cars in the Eastern U.S. because the bridges were all built with too little clearance. Fact-checkers encounter these offhand assertions all the time: a just-so statement with the ring of a thing that everybody knows. If you were to Google this type of niche knowledge, you might not find anything, and so the fact-checker operates most often as a reporter of the reporting. But after calling the railroad lines themselves, Murphy learned that in the year since the writer had filed the piece, a considerable number of bridges had been raised to allow freight through. The writer’s claim was “either too pessimistic to begin with or had changed in that year,” says Murphy. There are few forces more powerful in the media than a stubborn person on the phone investigating a doubt. It is precisely that thoroughness that makes peer-to-peer fact-checking matter more now in the age of A.I. Of course most large language models (LLMs) can’t yet make phone calls to freight lines, but if I ask Claude about Murphy’s rail bridges I may well still be told that nobody double-stacks rail cars in the Eastern U.S. That model can create a convincing, seemingly well-sourced sentence in a few seconds, but what it is not doing is actually checking the fact . Kelsey Lannin, a Seattle-based fact-checker, tells me that A.I is “very good at aping a confident intellectual on any given topic. But do any amount of work with it and you’ll quickly realize it’s a facade.” She says that it’s better to look at it like having an intern: “You give it an assignment, it gives you something back, and you [still] have to check it.” A.I. boosters may tell you that we’re just getting started, and assure us that this is the worst A.I. will ever be. Nevertheless, A.I. is still failing to produce accurate citations in more than 60 percent of tests, according to a 2025 Tow Center study . Prominent critics say it has nuked the effectiveness of Google and is “ destroying search, the internet and your brain. ” Models create a texture of verification, but they aren’t doing the analog process that makes verification real. If you see a bird out of your window, you can grab an Audubon guide and verify it. Feed a picture of that bird to an LLM and that model is neither “seeing” the chickadee nor “reading” from a primary source specifically. Models produce the most statistically likely next words, but unless prompted, there isn’t a step where Claude or Gemini confirms the truth of its response against the truth of the world. Credit: Andrey_Popov / Shutterstock Fact-checking’s collective response to changing times will continue to be a necessary governor, helping pace our accelerated information environment and dismantle false narratives that fuel polarization. These individual hallucinations and absent citations might seem like drops in a bucket, but they add up to create a rising tide of mistrust in a society already wary of the truthfulness of mainstream media . “What grieves me,” says Murphy, “is how many people think there aren’t [trusted sources].” Still, it is encouraging to see the fact-checking infrastructure responding by adapting to, and building defenses against, this flood. Sometimes, resistance looks like digging in. Inside the same Reporters’ Lab census that tallied closures, we learn that we’ve still got 437 active fact-checking projects around the world, which is just 27 below the all-time high and more than were operating in 2020. Many American newsrooms (North Dakota News Cooperative, CT Mirror in Connecticut and more) have agreed to work with Gigafact , an organization that publishes independently verified “fact briefs.” Wikipedia adopted a stronger A.I.-generated content policy earlier this year, banning LLM-generated content on the site, bar in certain circumstances. And as something becomes perceived to be scarce, it also becomes valuable: A 2026 Reuters study points toward an “increased demand for verification” from readers in a low-trust environment. The most encouraging turn of resistance may be in redirecting the machine back at the onslaught itself. Full Fact , the U.K.’s independent fact-checking charity, is now using A.I. systems to “detect and classify claims across millions of sentences,” per Reuters . A newer version attempts to “prebunk” instead of debunk, creating a model that prioritizes the most potentially damaging narratives for review. A Joint Research Centre study published in Nature investigated and concluded that debunking and prebunking interventions were successful and effective in reducing misinformation’s threats. Like any effort in inoculation, this effort will also need to be collective. At the end of last year, Scott Klein, then-publisher advocate at Newspack, predicted a “return to prioritizing open source collaboration, not as a luxury but as an existential imperative,” highlighting the need for a “show your work” ethos that will help journalism rebuild trust. Full Fact’s tools are being used now by more than 40 organizations across 30 countries, and importantly, the effort is mostly triage. Full Fact offers that the organization will “always keep human experts in the loop, partly to minimise the risks around bias and hallucinations that come with fully-automated systems but mostly because even the most advanced A.I. does not come close to human reasoning.” Wait, you're not a member yet? Join the Reasons to be Cheerful community by supporting our nonprofit publication and giving what you can. Join Cancel anytime Sierra Juarez, a fact-checker at NPR’s Planet Money and The Indicator , has another, simpler tip for resistance in the world of misinformation. “If you see something on your social media feed that your gut is telling you seems fishy,” she says, “try to find corroborating evidence in three different sources across different types of publications. Read broadly and try to identify common threads.” Bringing the fact-checker’s stubborn doubt to our daily engagement is available to anyone willing to take a minute before they share a post. Years after my Wikipedia crime spree, I’m heartened that there are fact-checkers out there guarding the bridge and encouraged by the durability of this work. Reports of the Truth’s demise have perhaps been greatly exaggerated. It can be slow and unglamorous, but fact-checking’s collective response to changing times will continue to be a necessary governor, helping pace our accelerated information environment and dismantle false narratives that fuel polarization. “There are,” says Murphy, “good soldiers … a cadre of us out there trying to fight the good fight.” The post Truth, Elections and the Questionable History of the Club Sandwich appeared first on Reasons to be Cheerful .

items.descriptionOriginal: Halloween may be known for its pumpkins, costumes, and haunted tales — but India has long celebrated its own versions of mystery and magic. Across the country, lamps glow through the night, dancers take on the forms of spirits, and stories of the unseen are shared by firelight. From Bengal's Bhoot Chaturdashi to Kerala's Theyyam , every region adds its own rhythm to this timeless fascination with light and darkness. Some mark the changing season, others honour folklore , but all capture that same mix of wonder and warmth — proof that India's festive calendar has its own kind of Halloween spirit. Though it may not be about trick or treating, wearing spooky costumes, or lighting pumpkins, these festivals draw striking parallels with Halloween — connecting people to folklore, community, and the idea that light always finds a way through darkness. Here's a look at five Indian traditions that echo the essence of Halloween, each with its own story, symbolism, and seasonal charm. 1. Bhoot Chaturdashi , also known as Bengali Halloween (West Bengal and Eastern India) When: A day before Diwali What people do: Families light 14 lamps at dusk to keep negative energies away. The lamps are placed in corners, near windows, and around the tulsi plant — illuminating every shadowed space in the home. It's also a night of storytelling, when elders share tales of ancestors and friendly spirits, filling homes with both curiosity and comfort. Why is it like Halloween? The festival centres around spirits and protection, much like Halloween's idea of keeping the dark at bay through light and play. 2. Kati Bihu (Assam) When: October / Around Diwali What people do: In rural Assam, Kati Bihu marks the transition between seasons and the start of the new agricultural cycle. Villagers light small lamps on bamboo poles in fields and granaries, hoping to protect crops from pests and bring good fortune to the harvest. Villagers light small lamps on bamboo poles in fields and granaries, hoping to protect crops from pests and bring good fortune to the harvest. (Image courtesy: assamtribune.com) This year, Kati Bihu coincided with Dhanteras , adding a shared glow across homes and fields. Why is it like Halloween? Though it celebrates the harvest, its essence lies in guarding against harm and illuminating darkness — an echo of Halloween's symbolic warmth amidst the chill. 3. Kartik Purnima (across North and West India) When: November What people do: As the full moon rises, rivers shimmer with hundreds of floating lamps. Families and communities gather near the water to celebrate light, gratitude, and the changing season. The night has a serene yet mystical feel — where reflection meets festivity, and the soft glow of lamps paints a picture of unity and peace. Why is it like Halloween? The moonlit night, glowing lamps, and celebration of transition carry the same sense of wonder that makes Halloween nights unforgettable. 4. Bhoota Kola (Tulu Nadu – Coastal Karnataka) When: Between December and May What people do: In the coastal districts of Karnataka, Bhoota Kola brings folklore to life through dramatic all-night performances. Performers, often from hereditary families, embody local spirit figures known as bhootas through elaborate costumes, striking makeup, and rhythmic dances. The event takes place under fire-lit skies and drumbeats, as villagers gather to watch tales of courage and justice unfold — part performance, part oral history. Why is it like Halloween? The transformation, the costumes, and the powerful night-time energy make Bhoota Kola India's own way of bridging the seen and unseen. 5. Theyyam (North Malabar, Kerala) When: October to May What people do: One of Kerala's most mesmerising ritual art forms, Theyyam combines dance, theatre, and transformation. Performers adorn vibrant face paint, ornate costumes, and towering headgear, embodying ancestral or mythic figures in a trance-like state. Like Halloween's symbolic costumes and storytelling, Theyyam celebrates transformation and mystery. The community gathers around as the performer, now in full transformation, narrates stories through movement, rhythm, and firelight — a living piece of folklore. Why is it like Halloween? Like Halloween's symbolic costumes and storytelling, Theyyam celebrates transformation and mystery — with its roots firmly planted in art and heritage. Source: ' What is Bhoot Chaturdashi also known as Bengali Halloween? How is it celebrated? ': by Ahana Bhattacharya, Published on 18 October 2025. items.descriptionOriginal: Running one of the world’s most powerful electron microscopes used to take weeks of training. At Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, researchers can now describe an experiment in plain English and let an AI agent run it. The system, called TEM Agent, was built at the Molecular Foundry, a U.S. Department of Energy user facility at Berkeley Lab. It controls a transmission electron microscope, an instrument that shows where atoms sit in a material, which determines how strong the material is, how it conducts electricity, how a battery stores energy and how a drug binds to a cell. A microscope that outpaced its users The Molecular Foundry’s microscopes can image structures roughly half the size of a hydrogen atom, and scientists from universities and companies travel there to use them. The learning curve is steep. Some visiting researchers arrive with a semester of electron microscopy coursework and still need weeks of hands-on training. Even experts struggle with the data: one detector can produce about 700 gigabytes in 15 seconds, far too fast to process by hand. The result is a bottleneck. The equipment keeps getting more powerful, but the number of people who can run and analyze it expertly can’t keep up. From factory line to conversation The team already had automated routines for repetitive jobs, such as imaging large numbers of nanoparticles. But those worked like a factory line, said Peter Ercius, the staff scientist who led the study. They did exactly what they were programmed to do, broke when something unexpected happened and couldn’t be changed by anyone who isn’t a robotics engineer. Instead of starting over, the team rewrote those routines in the Model Context Protocol, an open standard that gives an AI a fixed set of specific, pre-written actions rather than open-ended control. With that toolkit, TEM Agen t can string steps together, even for requests no one programmed. “It was pretty amazing that it worked out of the box,” Ercius said. Tomography and ptychography on request Researchers describe an experiment in plain English, and the agent adjusts magnification, tilts the sample, refocuses the beam and chains together dozens of small steps. The team tested it on electron tomography, which rebuilds a 3D view of a sample from tilted images and can take hours. Early on, the agent confused rotating the sample with rotating the scan direction, and a short written explanation fixed it. Stephanie Ribet, a research scientist at the Molecular Foundry, then pushed it into more experimental territory, including ptychography, a technique that reconstructs high-resolution images from diffraction patterns and typically takes significant expertise to set up. Connecting an AI to scientific hardware is harder than connecting it to literature or data pipelines, she said, and the protocol gave the team a way to bridge the two. Linked to supercomputing and a data platform The agent is also tied to the National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center, a DOE supercomputing facility, and to Crucible, a Molecular Foundry data platform that organizes experiment metadata. Raw data can be processed in seconds instead of hours, and researchers can ask what settings they used on a sample weeks earlier without digging through files or notebooks. Morgan Wall, who leads Crucible’s development, said users can talk in natural language to one interface instead of juggling five scripts on five computers. What comes next The approach could extend to other instruments with an open interface, and Wall’s team is helping other nanoscale research centers adopt Crucible. The aim, the release says, is not to replace expertise but to extend it, giving new and experienced researchers a faster path from idea to experiment. Ercius expects such assistants to democratize this type of work. The research was supported by the DOE Office of Science. The work was published in journal npj Computational Materials .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Funding for Indigenous-Led Forest Conservation Gets a New Global Platform Reading Time: 3 minutes Funding for Indigenous-led forest conservation just became easier, as a new UNDP-hosted platform connects private companies and philanthropies directly with the communities protecting many of the world’s most critical forests. Funding for Indigenous-led forest conservation has long faced a structural gap. Indigenous Peoples steward roughly one third of the world’s tropical forests, yet they receive comparatively little political recognition or financial support for that role. Recent climate summits have repeatedly called for Indigenous access to forest tenure rights and climate finance, but turning those pledges into action has proven difficult. A new initiative, Forest Guardians Invest , aims to close that gap directly. Hosted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the platform connects private companies, impact investors, and philanthropies with vetted Indigenous-led conservation and bioeconomy projects. Rather than routing funds through layers of intermediaries, the platform creates a more direct financial pathway. Tropical forests play an outsized role in global climate goals. These ecosystems support simultaneous action on climate change, biodiversity loss, and sustainable land management in ways few other landscapes can match. Protecting them effectively requires working with the people who already know these forests best. Many private companies and philanthropies are genuinely willing to fund forest protection through direct partnerships with Indigenous communities. What they typically lack is a reliable, efficient mechanism to do so at scale. Forest Guardians Invest positions itself as that missing mechanism, built specifically around respect for Indigenous rights and international standards. Three core functions define how the funding for Indigenous-led forest conservation platform operates. First, it facilitates financial partnerships between Indigenous Peoples and private companies, ensuring every agreement complies with human rights protections and recognized ESG standards. Second, it monitors private investments in Indigenous-led projects to confirm they deliver the environmental and economic outcomes both parties agreed upon. The platform’s third function focuses on long-term scale. Forest Guardians Invest builds a pipeline of bankable, Indigenous-led bioeconomy projects across forest territories, each with demonstrated climate, biodiversity, and economic results. That pipeline gives investors a clearer picture of opportunities beyond a single pilot project. Partnership models built around free, prior, and informed consent anchor the platform’s approach to Indigenous rights. This framework ensures Indigenous communities retain genuine decision-making power over how their territories and resources get used. Companies gain a trusted gateway to opportunities already vetted for impact and ethical compliance. One early example illustrates how this model works in practice. UNDP partnered with coffee company Lavazza to certify and market the first-ever deforestation-free coffee sourced from Ecuador. That pilot project is now being scaled to additional countries, offering a template for how similar partnerships might expand elsewhere. Harvesting coffee, part of a certified deforestation-free supply chain that shows what funding for Indigenous-led forest conservation can look like in practice. Photo by Carlos Felipe Ramírez Mesa on Unsplash. Founding partner Sacred Forests contributed both funding and a working model during the platform’s design phase. Their approach treats forest conservation itself as a service worth compensating directly, rather than folding it into broader carbon-offset accounting that often overlooks community-level impact. Seed funding from partners like Sacred Forests helped move Forest Guardians Invest from concept to functioning platform. The kind of on-the-ground work this funding for Indigenous-led forest conservation aims to support is already visible across the Amazon. In Brazil’s Maranhão state, a group of Guajajara women known as the Forest Warriors patrol more than 172,000 hectares of the Caru Indigenous Land. They monitor illegal logging, fight wildfires, and combine traditional ecological knowledge with modern tools like drones and GPS mapping. Efforts like theirs demonstrate both the value and the vulnerability of Indigenous-led conservation. Communities already carry out sophisticated, effective forest protection work, often with minimal external funding or formal recognition. Connecting that work to reliable financial support could meaningfully expand its reach and sustainability. Companies and philanthropies interested in engaging with the platform can apply to explore partnership opportunities directly through UNDP’s Climate and Forests initiative. Each partnership gets built around measurable outcomes, giving funders concrete evidence of the climate and biodiversity impact their investment produces. Funding for Indigenous-led forest conservation through platforms like this represents a shift in how global climate finance operates. Rather than treating Indigenous communities as beneficiaries of external programs, this model positions them as direct partners and innovators. That distinction may prove essential for protecting the forests the planet depends on most. The post Funding for Indigenous-Led Forest Conservation Gets a New Global Platform appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News New Map Reveals Natural Forest Regeneration in Tropical Regions Could Absorb 23 Years of Global Emissions Reading Time: 3 minutes A groundbreaking map identifies 215 million hectares suited for natural forest regeneration in tropical regions, capable of sequestering 23.4 gigatons of carbon. For decades, tree planting dominated forest restoration efforts worldwide, despite mounting evidence that a quieter, less expensive alternative often works better. Natural forest regeneration in tropical regions, allowing degraded land to recover on its own with minimal human intervention, frequently produces more biodiverse, resilient forests than plantation-style restoration under similar conditions. Until now, researchers lacked detailed, high-resolution data showing precisely where this natural recovery process holds the greatest promise. A Nature Ecology and Evolution study closed that gap, producing the first model mapping natural forest regeneration potential in tropical regions across every tropical forested country and biome on Earth. Built on remote sensing analysis identifying actual patches of natural forest regrowth between 2000 and 2016, rather than relying on coarse estimates or expert guesswork as previous studies had, the map offers unprecedented precision for targeting restoration investment. The results are striking. Researchers estimate 215 million hectares, an area larger than the entire country of Mexico, hold genuine potential for natural forest regeneration in tropical regions. Left to recover naturally over 30 years, this land could sequester an estimated 23.4 gigatons of above-ground carbon, roughly equivalent to more than two decades of current global emissions from fossil fuels and industry combined. Five countries account for more than half of this global potential. Brazil leads with over 20% of total regeneration potential, followed by Indonesia at nearly 14%, then China, Mexico, and Colombia, rounding out the top five nations that collectively represent 52% of the opportunity worldwide. This concentration suggests that even modest policy shifts within a handful of countries could unlock outsized climate and biodiversity benefits. What distinguishes natural forest regeneration in tropical regions from active planting is cost-effectiveness paired with ecological quality. Rather than purchasing seedlings, preparing sites, and maintaining plantations, natural regeneration often requires simply removing barriers preventing forest recovery, invasive species, unmanaged livestock grazing, or encroaching agriculture, then allowing existing seed banks, root systems, and nearby forest patches to do the rest. Research consistently shows this approach yields forests with greater species diversity and more resilient ecosystem function compared to plantation alternatives. Integrating Indigenous knowledge and securing land rights within these territories increasingly stands out as essential to translating mapped potential into genuine forest recovery. Communities that have sustainably managed these landscapes for generations bring practical understanding of local conditions that purely technical restoration planning cannot replicate on its own. Natural forest regeneration in tropical regions succeeds most reliably near existing forest patches and within territories managed by Indigenous Peoples, whose land stewardship researchers say is essential to translating mapped regeneration potential into genuine, lasting forest recovery. Photo by Bill Salazar on Pexels. The map reveals fine-scale spatial variation researchers say is critical for effective planning. Regeneration potential clusters strongly near existing forest patches, since seed dispersal and ecological connectivity heavily influence whether cleared land can recover naturally. This granular detail lets governments and conservation organizations distinguish between land where natural forest regeneration in tropical regions will likely succeed unaided and land that requires more intensive intervention or active planting. Beyond carbon sequestration, restoring tropical forests at this scale carries far-reaching consequences for biodiversity conservation, since tropical forests harbor a disproportionate share of Earth’s terrestrial species diversity. Millions of livelihoods across forested tropical nations also depend directly on healthy forest ecosystems for food, water regulation, and economic activity, so successful regeneration delivers benefits that extend well beyond atmospheric carbon accounting. Researchers emphasize that the map is intended as a decision-support tool rather than a final policy prescription. Natural forest regeneration in tropical regions succeeds only when paired with appropriate governance structures, including payment-for-ecosystem-services schemes and stronger frameworks that compensate communities for environmental stewardship. The overlap between high-potential regeneration zones and Indigenous Peoples’ territories adds further complexity, since these communities often lack formal land recognition despite serving as effective forest stewards in practice. As nations pursue ambitious global restoration commitments under frameworks addressing both climate change and biodiversity loss, this map offers something previously unavailable: precise, evidence-based guidance on where natural forest regeneration in tropical regions could deliver the greatest return on conservation investment. Rather than treating forest restoration as a uniform global strategy, the research points to a more targeted approach, one that recognizes that some degraded tropical land wants only the chance to heal itself, provided the barriers standing in its way are finally removed. The post New Map Reveals Natural Forest Regeneration in Tropical Regions Could Absorb 23 Years of Global Emissions appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: Από τις νέες θεραπευτικές επιλογές για τις αιματολογικές κακοήθειες μέχρι την αξιοποίηση της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης στην καθημερινή κλινική πράξη, η Αιματολογία βρίσκεται σε μια περίοδο σημαντικών επιστημονικών εξελίξεων. Οι δυνατότητες που ανοίγονται για την ακριβέστερη διάγνωση, την εξατομίκευση των θεραπειών και τη βελτίωση της φροντίδας των ασθενών θα αποτελέσουν βασικούς άξονες του 37ου Πανελλήνιου Αιματολογικού Συνεδρίου. Όπως αναφέρει σε ανακοίνωσή της η Ελληνική Αιματολογική Εταιρεία (ΕΑΕ) , η διοργάνωση θα πραγματοποιηθεί από τις 5 έως τις 7 Νοεμβρίου 2026, στο Συνεδριακό Κέντρο «Ι. Βελλίδης» της HELEXPO, στη Θεσσαλονίκη, με τη συμμετοχή επιστημόνων από την Ελλάδα και το εξωτερικό. Το φετινό συνέδριο έχει ιδιαίτερη σημασία, καθώς συμπίπτει με τη συμπλήρωση 65 χρόνων από την ίδρυση της ΕΑΕ, με κεντρικό μήνυμα «65 χρόνια ΕΑΕ: Συνδέοντας Γενιές, Ανοίγοντας Ορίζοντες». Νέες θεραπείες και εξατομικευμένη αντιμετώπιση Σύμφωνα με την ΕΑΕ, ιδιαίτερη έμφαση στο επιστημονικό πρόγραμμα θα δοθεί στις σύγχρονες θεραπευτικές στρατηγικές για τη λευχαιμία , τα λεμφώματα και το πολλαπλό μυέλωμα, καθώς και στις εξελίξεις στη μεταμόσχευση αιμοποιητικών κυττάρων. Στο επίκεντρο θα βρεθούν επίσης οι κυτταρικές θεραπείες CAR-T , οι οποίες αξιοποιούν τροποποιημένα ανοσοκύτταρα του ασθενούς για την αντιμετώπιση συγκεκριμένων μορφών καρκίνου του αίματος, αλλά και οι νέες δυνατότητες της ανοσοθεραπείας και των γονιδιακών τεχνολογιών. Παράλληλα, θα εξεταστούν οι προοπτικές της εξατομικευμένης ιατρικής, με στόχο τη διαμόρφωση θεραπευτικών προσεγγίσεων που ανταποκρίνονται καλύτερα στα ιδιαίτερα χαρακτηριστικά κάθε ασθενούς. Το πρόγραμμα περιλαμβάνει ακόμη θέματα που αφορούν την ασφάλεια των μεταγγίσεων , την εργαστηριακή διάγνωση, την αιμόσταση, την παιδιατρική Αιματολογία και τη συνολική φροντίδα των ασθενών. Τεχνητή νοημοσύνη και ψηφιακές τεχνολογίες στην υγεία Ξεχωριστή θέση στη φετινή διοργάνωση καταλαμβάνει ο ρόλος της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης και των ψηφιακών τεχνολογιών στη σύγχρονη Αιματολογία. Όπως επισημαίνει η ΕΑΕ, το συνέδριο θα εξετάσει τις δυνατότητες αξιοποίησης αυτών των εργαλείων στην κλινική πράξη, αλλά και στον ευρύτερο εκσυγχρονισμό των υπηρεσιών υγείας. Στο πλαίσιο αυτό, έχει προγραμματιστεί συζήτηση μεταξύ φορέων υγείας για τη συμβολή των ψηφιακών τεχνολογιών στην οργάνωση και τη λειτουργία των υπηρεσιών υγείας και της αιμοδοσίας. Μέσα από διαλέξεις, εκπαιδευτικά συμπόσια και επιστημονικές αντιπαραθέσεις, θα συζητηθούν επίσης σύνθετα κλινικά περιστατικά και θεραπευτικά διλήμματα που αντιμετωπίζουν οι αιματολόγοι στην καθημερινή πρακτική. Η συμμετοχή του προέδρου της Αμερικανικής Αιματολογικής Εταιρείας Μία από τις σημαντικές στιγμές του συνεδρίου, σύμφωνα με τους διοργανωτές, θα είναι η Διάλεξη του Προσκεκλημένου Προέδρου, με ομιλητή τον Robert S. Negrin, πρόεδρο της Αμερικανικής Αιματολογικής Εταιρείας (ASH). Η ομιλία του θα επικεντρωθεί στον ρόλο των ρυθμιστικών Τ κυττάρων στη βελτίωση των εκβάσεων μετά από αλλογενή μεταμόσχευση αιμοποιητικών κυττάρων, ένα πεδίο με ιδιαίτερο ερευνητικό ενδιαφέρον. Στην ίδια συνεδρία θα παρουσιαστούν και οι βραβευμένες επιστημονικές εργασίες, αναδεικνύοντας την ερευνητική δραστηριότητα της ελληνικής αιματολογικής κοινότητας. Νέα γενιά αιματολόγων και πρακτική εκπαίδευση Η συμπλήρωση 65 χρόνων από την ίδρυση της ΕΑΕ συνοδεύεται από μια νέα πρωτοβουλία: τη δημιουργία της Ομάδας Νέων Ελλήνων Αιματολόγων (ΟΝΕΑ). Στόχος της, όπως αναφέρεται στην ανακοίνωση, είναι η ενίσχυση της συμμετοχής των νεότερων αιματολόγων στις επιστημονικές και θεσμικές δραστηριότητες της Εταιρείας. Η ΟΝΕΑ θα συμμετάσχει στο συνέδριο με ειδικό συμπόσιο, που φιλοδοξεί να ενισχύσει την ανταλλαγή γνώσεων και τον διάλογο μεταξύ διαφορετικών γενεών επιστημόνων. Μία ακόμη καινοτομία της διοργάνωσης είναι η ένταξη, για πρώτη φορά, εξειδικευμένων πρακτικών εργαστηρίων (workshops). Η θεματολογία τους εκτείνεται πέρα από την αμιγώς ιατρική γνώση και περιλαμβάνει τις κλινικές μελέτες, τις δεξιότητες επικοινωνίας, τη διαχείριση συγκρούσεων και την επαγγελματική εξέλιξη των αιματολόγων. Με τη συμμετοχή επιστημόνων από διαφορετικά πεδία και γενιές, η ΕΑΕ επιδιώκει το συνέδριο να αποτελέσει χώρο ανταλλαγής επιστημονικής γνώσης και ενίσχυσης της συνεργασίας, με τελικό στόχο τη βελτίωση της περίθαλψης των ασθενών με αιματολογικά νοσήματα. Περισσότερες πληροφορίες και αναλυτικό πρόγραμμα: www.eaecongress2026.gr Διαβάστε επίσης Καινοτόμος ανοσοθεραπεία οδήγησε σε ύφεση ανθεκτικό καρκίνο ήπατος σε 3χρονο ασθενή Βιταμίνη C: Μπορεί να «φρενάρει» τη λευχαιμία πριν εκδηλωθεί; Τι έδειξε νέα μελέτη Λέμφωμα: Οι προκλήσεις για τους ασθενείς στην Ελλάδα – Τα συμπτώματα που προδίδουν τη νόσο

items.descriptionOriginal: This story is part of "India Invented This?" — The Better India's weekly trivia series that uncovers the Indian minds, ideas and innovations behind inventions that have shaped the way we live. From ingenious solutions created by scientists and engineers to technologies developed in response to some of India's biggest challenges, each story goes beyond the invention to explore the problem it solved, the impact it created and why it still matters today. On a winter morning in Delhi, the skyline can almost disappear behind a grey haze. The air feels heavy, eyes begin to sting, and even a short walk outdoors can become uncomfortable. For millions of residents, this is a familiar part of life during the city's pollution season. But what if scientists could predict when the air is likely to get worse — before the haze settles in? That is the question Dr Sachin Ghude, a scientist at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune, has been working to answer. Winter pollution can blanket Delhi in haze, making it harder for residents to breathe comfortably and increasing the need for timely air-quality warnings. Photograph: ( BBC) Ghude has played a leading role in developing India's Air Quality Early Warning System (AQEWS), which can forecast extreme pollution events in Delhi up to 72 hours in advance. Developed through a collaborative effort involving IITM, the India Meteorological Department and the National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting, the system gives authorities valuable time to prepare for deteriorating air quality. Predicting pollution before it arrives Air pollution is not caused by a single source. Vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, construction dust and crop-residue burning can all contribute to the problem. Weather conditions also play a crucial role: when winds are weak and the atmosphere prevents pollutants from dispersing, pollution can build up near the ground. Understanding how these factors interact is central to Ghude's work in atmospheric chemistry and air-quality modelling. Think of AQEWS as a weather forecast for the air we breathe. While a conventional weather forecast predicts rain or temperature changes, this system also calculates how pollutants are likely to move, react and accumulate in the atmosphere. AQEWS combines weather forecasts, satellite data, ground-based monitoring and emissions estimates to predict how pollution levels may change. Photograph: ( AQI.in ) To do this, it combines observations from ground-based monitoring stations with satellite information, weather forecasts and estimates of emissions from different sources. Advanced computer models then simulate how atmospheric conditions and pollutants may change over the next three days. The result is a forecast of air quality, including pollutants such as fine particulate matter (PM2.5), which can penetrate deep into the lungs. Why a 72-hour warning matters The system's biggest contribution is the time it gives authorities to respond. When pollution levels rise sharply, officials may need to consider measures such as restricting construction activities or curbing certain industrial operations under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). A forecast issued in advance can help them prepare for these interventions instead of reacting only after air quality has deteriorated. The system was launched in October 2018 to predict extreme pollution episodes and provide early alerts. By forecasting severe pollution up to three days ahead, the system gives authorities time to consider preventive measures before air quality worsens. Photograph: ( The Indian Express ) The science has also moved towards more detailed forecasts. IITM has implemented an operational air-quality forecasting model for Delhi at a resolution of 400 metres, using satellite and surface observations alongside advanced modelling techniques. This allows forecasts to capture local variations in pollution more closely than a single city-wide average. Such forecasts do not eliminate pollution on their own. Their effectiveness depends on how authorities use the information and how successfully they tackle the sources of emissions. Where is all this pollution coming from? Forecasting when pollution will worsen is only part of the challenge. Scientists must also understand where it comes from. Different pollution sources leave different chemical signatures. By studying these alongside atmospheric conditions, researchers can better estimate which sources contribute to poor air quality and help policymakers identify more targeted interventions. This is an important part of the broader scientific effort to make air-quality management more precise, moving beyond simply measuring pollution towards understanding what drives it. Studying the chemical signatures of pollutants helps researchers identify their likely sources and supports more targeted air-quality management. Photograph: ( IITM ) For Ghude, whose research connects atmospheric chemistry with air quality, human health, vegetation and climate, this work brings complex science closer to everyday public needs. A forecast cannot promise that tomorrow's sky will be clear. But knowing that pollution may worsen three days from now gives authorities an opportunity to prepare — and gives the rest of us a clearer picture of the air we are about to breathe. Sources: 'Dr. Sachin D Ghude' by ileaps 'Impact of Biomass Burning on Fine Aerosol Chemistry and Aging Processes in the Indo‐Gangetic Plain' by Sachin D Ghude for Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres. 'Delhi: Scientists look to trace exact source of pollution to help improve air quality' by Kushagra Dixit for The Times of India, Published on 29 January 2022. 'IITM releases documentary on air quality warning system for Delhi' by Indian Express, Published on 19 February 2021.

items.description: Ένας άντρας στο Μίσιγκαν περνούσε μια ιδιαίτερα δύσκολη μέρα. Ως υπάλληλος αργά το βράδυ στο κατάστημα παράδοσης για την πίτσα Red Baron, ο «Walt Z» δούλευε πολλές, εξαντλητικές ώρες, μάζευε πίτσα στον διάδρομο παγωμένου φαγητού. Ωστόσο, αυτό δεν τον εμπόδισε να χαιρετήσει έναν πελάτη με ευγένεια όταν του ζητήθηκε η ώρα. Τα πράγματα γρήγορα πήραν τροπή από εκεί. Σε ένα κλιπ που κάνει τους γύρους…
items.descriptionOriginal: A man in Michigan was having an especially hard day. As a late night store delivery worker for Red Baron pizza , “Walt Z” was working long, exhausting hours, stocking pizza in the frozen food aisle. Yet this didn’t stop him from greeting a customer with kindness when asked the time. Things quickly took a turn from there. In a clip making the rounds, we see him as he’s approached by a guy asking a question. When he pulls out his phone, the man “pretends” to steal ten dollars by using Apple Pay. Turns out the whole exchange had been a poorly thought-out “prank” from someone trying to get online clicks, and is filming/streaming the exchange live. View this post on Instagram At his wit’s end The worker was simply at his wit’s end. He essentially—and quite understandably—gets emotional and angry, as he pleads his case to the man filming. “Are you recording me right now,” he asks, while walking toward the front of the store. The streamer doesn’t let up, even when the employee seems visibly devastated. The streamer maintains that it’s “just a joke”. But it wasn’t a joke to this hardworking man. “It’s not a joke to me, okay? I don’t have time for this crap right now, okay? My life is hard enough as it is. I’ve got kids at home who went to bed without me right now.” He raises his voice, as his own words begin to hit home. “I was supposed to be home an hour ago. I’m still out here working. And I got to get up at 5 in the morning and do ten more stores! So this is not a joke to me!” Once it sets in that again, this is being filmed, he realizes there may be consequences. “And now I’m gonna get kicked out of the store BECAUSE OF YOU! Not funny!” The streamer apologizes, but it’s too late. The employee continues, “I’ve got a mortgage. And I’ve got four kids at home! So not funny!” It’s gut-wrenching to watch, maybe because so many of us have been there. Hanging on by a thread, trying to juggle our lives. Most likely, the prankster didn’t mean to set off such heavy emotions. But it’s a huge reminder that we never know what’s going on with someone on any given day. A wonderful turn But this story takes an incredible turn for the wonderful. Once the video went live, there was an outpouring of support for the employee. A man named Luke Oakenshield, without even knowing the worker’s name, started a GoFundMe in his honor. Oakenshield explains, “I do not know the worker personally and am actively searching for his contact information so I can make sure he receives the funds directly. Any aid in finding this man would be of the greatest help. I will not be receiving any of the money, as this is intended for the worker. God bless.” Standing up for the working person He also explains why he was so moved to help. “This fundraiser is about standing up for a working person who is busting their butt and should not have to fear losing stability because someone wanted content and clicks. If you can, please donate and share to help push back against rage-bait harassment and show this worker that people care.” Care, they did. In just a day, the GoFundMe at raised over $410,000 and it’s growing quickly. The page was updated to share they found the employee and that he’s over the moon. Oakenshield shares, “THE WORKER HAS BEEN FOUND! Walt Z out of Michigan sends a heartfelt thank you, and is absolutely blown away by how much people have cared over this. They are requesting privacy, and GoFundMe is taking the lead in transferring all of this to him. You’re all rock stars, and it shows.” Employee of the month But there’s more. Since there was fear that Walt might lose his job, Red Baron Pizza not only confirmed that he still worked for them, but that he was receiving the “employee of the month” title. They add, “He’s still here. He’s got a fan club. Including us.” View this post on Instagram It was just one of those days. Some online are calling it his Falling Down moment (referring to the film wherein Michael Douglas’s final straw is McDonald’s not serving breakfast after 10:00am). It didn’t end well for Douglas. But for Walt…now there’s proof that there are still total strangers who have his back. As for the content creator, reportedly he has deleted his social media. Perhaps this chain of events can have a positive effect on his life too. Who knows? Maybe Red Baron, who seem like a pretty standup company, is hiring. The post A Red Baron worker was devastated by a mean viral ‘prank.’ Strangers stepped in and changed his life. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: The world’s first legged inspection robot for explosive atmospheres is now set to be delivered to its customers. Called ANYmal X, the robot uses an advanced industrial AI stack to execute routine autonomous inspections in hazardous environments. Developed by ANYbotics, the robot is now being shipped to several oil, gas, and chemical industry leaders, including Equinor and DSM-Firmenich. A legged robot could never be made safe for explosive atmospheres “Four years of pioneering engineering with more than ten patents went into ANYmal X,” said Péter Fankhauser, co-founder and CEO of ANYbotics. “Many experts thought a legged robot could never be made safe for explosive atmospheres. Oil, gas and chemical plants are among the most hazardous and most costly places to operate. That makes them the prime case for physical and industrial AI, yet until now the areas that matter most were off-limits to robots like ours. That changes today.” ANYmal X automates high-risk inspection rounds without requiring any facility modifications, navigating complex industrial environments such as steep stairs and narrow walkways. Its integrated thermal, visual, acoustic, and gas sensors detect overheating, leaks, abnormal noise, and equipment wear, logging every reading directly to its corresponding asset. This gives reliability engineers a standardized baseline to track asset health over time, enabling teams to spot early signs of wear and intervene before minor issues escalate into costly plant shutdowns, according to a press release. Comprehensive ignition-risk assessment for ANYmal X robot’s service life ANYmal X was engineered from the ground up to comply with the oil, gas, and chemical sectors’ strictest safety standards. ANYbotics performed a comprehensive ignition-risk assessment for ANYmal X’s service life and implemented safeguards for each potential ignition source. Each of its components has been designed to minimize ignition risk. ANYmal X’s AI computer and inspection equipment are enclosed in nitrogen-filled, sealed chambers. Non-metallic shells insulate metallic components, conductive feet provide grounding, and automatic cutoffs monitor temperature. All twelve leg actuators and its battery are protected by flameproof casings. “We asked one question over and over: which credible event in the life of a walking robot could create an ignition source, and how do we make sure it never does?” says Andrea Corda, CTO of ANYbotics. “Working closely with the certification bodies, we answered that question component by component. The result is a new explosion-protection approach for an entire class of autonomous mobile robots.” ANYmal X’s onboard software monitors the robot’s condition before, during, and after each mission. It also tests durability against shock, vibration, corrosion, solar radiation, and salt mist to ensure all protective measures function properly in normal use. “A certified robot is only the entry ticket for inspecting oil, gas, and chemicals facilities. ANYmal X is a complete end-to-end inspection solution built for performance, safety, and security. It combines autonomous navigation, industrial AI for data interpretation, and integrations that convert findings directly into maintenance work orders. Today, more than 50 power, metals, and materials customers use this system to run over 120,000 autonomous inspections every month,” added Thierry Obédé, Chief Revenue Officer at ANYbotics. In operation, ANYmal X runs on Shift, ANYbotics’ operations platform for autonomous industrial inspection. Shift schedules robot missions, organizes findings by asset and helps maintenance teams track changes over time. It connects inspection findings with the plant systems teams already use, including SAP, Yokogawa and SLB. To ensure top-tier data protection, the whole system is developed and operated under ISO 27001 standards, as per the release.
